messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The current bug report states that LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer ignores the VectorialConvergenceChecker parameter passed to it, causing difficulties when users try to specify custom stopping criteria. Inspection of the constructor for LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer shows only a default constructor which does not accept or set a VectorialConvergenceChecker. It initializes some default values but does not seem to have any mechanism to accept or utilize a user-provided convergence checker.

In contrast, the superclass AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer sets a default convergence checker in its constructor but does not show any override or respect of an external VectorialConvergenceChecker in the subclass. Because the subclass may not provide a way to pass in and store an externally supplied convergence checker, any parameter passed likely has no effect, resulting in the observed behavior that the passed VectorialConvergenceChecker is ignored.

This diagnosis explains why the optimization calls in tests relying on custom convergence checkers will fail or behave as if the checker is not set, matching the user report that the parameter is ignored by LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer.

Therefore, the root cause is that LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer does not have a constructor or setter logic to accept and apply the given VectorialConvergenceChecker, leading to default or no usage of a custom checker.

The failing test, testing minimization with JennrichSampsonFunction, is related as it exercises optimization but may rely on custom convergence checking which is not respected.

Recent bug reports do not directly relate to this convergence checker issue and focus on mathematical correctness or input checking, so they can be disregarded here.

Overall, ensuring that the LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer properly takes and uses the VectorialConvergenceChecker passed in construction or via a setter is needed to fix this bug.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
